niche.diet: Dissolved iron-sulfate, suspended calcite dust, chemosynthetic biofilm

chains.trait: Ventral cilia-band rides slow brine flow
links: Darcy flow runs centimetres per year
Passive drifting wastes energy in high-viscosity brine
Rock matrix limits permeability to 1e-17 m2

skill.effect: The creature rides the slow brine flow across fractured ground, gliding swiftly so you can traverse broken terrain without delay.

chains.weakness: Stops instantly if fluid flow reverses direction
observe: Tracks visible in fresh calcite dust

journal.en: They do not swim; they surf the crust.

plausibility.summary: Rename the root mechanism from surfing cm/yr flow to ciliary creeping plus local pumping: cilia let it hold station on a fracture wall and draw brine across the ventral biofilm; treat the 56-hour tidal strain (F4) as a weak timing cue for aperture pulses, not a fast current. Weakness becomes 'lose position and withdraw when flow reverses or pressure drops', not instant stop.

chains.trait: Dorsal calcite-crushing jaws harvest sealed minerals
links: Seals fractures and traps redox nutrients

journal.en: They crack the planet’s scars to feed.

temperament: Docile grazer, easily startled by pressure drops
secrets: If you play the 56-hour tidal drum, they will stop moving and listen.
Their jaw dust can be harvested to temporarily soften nearby calcite walls.
moments: When a fracture seals, the herd presses bellies to the rock and waits centuries for the stone to crack open again.

journal.en: The crust is a maze, and they are the compass.
